note: What build_release.py packages and declares for the first release (PLT-11, D-25): the shared chat code captured by PLT-9 and PLT-15 and its SKILL.md guidance. Format identifiers without an embedded version are documented baseline identifiers: the build changes no serialized byte.

package.name: plateia-chat
package.summary: Plateia's shared project chat: client, identities, pchat, the chat bridge and log rotation

platforms.verified: Linux in CI (build-test); macOS by one recorded run on the owner's machine

interpreter.note: the only pinned dependency: the chat code uses the standard library alone, and requires its sqlite3 module (the outbox authority, #19)

host_modules.name: weechat
host_modules.provided_by: WeeChat, to the scripts it loads
host_modules.used_by: role_colors.py, which falls back to no colors when the module is missing

formats.name: irc-client
formats.covers: pchat and chatlib: IRC with IRCv3 sasl (PLAIN), message-tags, batch and draft/multiline; +draft/reply on posts and +draft/react=ack TAGMSG acknowledgements

formats.name: irc-bridge
formats.covers: chat-bridge: the client capabilities plus server-time, account-tag, draft/chathistory (CHATHISTORY AFTER, pages of 1000) and draft/event-playback

formats.name: post-text
formats.covers: the [type request-id] prefix, the ' — authority: msgid=<id>' suffix and the '… ' continuation of a split post

formats.name: cmux-cli
formats.covers: the cmux commands binding, identities, agentcli and the bridge run (sessions list, agent messages, typed prompts)

formats.name: launchd-query
formats.covers: `launchctl print gui/<uid>/<label>`, which pchat status and rotate-logs read for a service's state and process ID

formats.name: process-table
formats.covers: `ps -o lstart=|comm=|ppid= -p <pid>`, which binding reads to identify an agent's process

formats.name: open-files
formats.covers: `lsof -a -p <pid> -Ffn`: identities.process_metadata() reads its f (descriptor) and n (name) field records for a process's working directory and its provider session, from an open thread-writer-locks/<uuid>.lock or rollout-*-<uuid>.jsonl name

formats.name: service-signal
formats.covers: rotate-logs sends SIGHUP to a log's service (Ergo's rehash) so it reopens its log

formats.name: agent-run-environment
formats.covers: CHAT_AGENT_ID, CHAT_AS, CHAT_CHANNEL and CHAT_REQUEST_ID: set by `pchat agent run` for the process it runs, and read by pchat, agentcli and runstore

formats.name: outbox-authority
formats.covers: the request protocol on $CHAT_STATE/outbox.sock between pchat, agentcli and the bridge's outbox authority (#19): one request and one reply per connection, each a 4-byte big-endian length then a JSON object whose v field names the version, and the peer credentials the bridge reads from that socket

formats.name: boot-id
formats.covers: /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, or `sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid`: the boot identifier the outbox authority compares to tell that a writer is gone

formats.name: tcp-sockets
formats.covers: a writer's TCP local ports, from /proc/<pid>/fd and /proc/net/tcp, or `lsof -a -p <pid> -iTCP -Fn -P -n`: what the outbox authority reads to tell that a writer's connection is closed

formats.name: ntfy-push
formats.covers: the bridge's content-free push to the owner's configured ntfy URL

formats.name: chat-config
formats.covers: read by every command; written by identities.register() when it provisions an account, records an identity's role or adds an assistant

formats.name: outbox
formats.path: $CHAT_STATE/outbox.jsonl, outbox.lock, outbox.claimed-*.jsonl, outbox.d/ (fallback files) and outbox.d/tmp/
formats.covers: outbox/1: the legacy rows of outbox.jsonl and its claim files, read only, which carry no version; outbox/2: one immutable fallback file per queued call in outbox.d/, whose v field names it

formats.name: outbox-db
formats.path: $CHAT_STATE/outbox.db with its -wal (and -shm) files, outbox.flush.lock, outbox.authority.lock, outbox.sock, outbox-status.json
formats.covers: the outbox's one SQLite authority (#19), opened and written by the bridge alone (writer_model bridge-exclusive/1); its version is the meta table's schema row

formats.name: weechat-role-colors
formats.path: WeeChat options weechat.look.nick_color_force and the role_colors script's own plugin option 'managed' (plugins.var.python.role_colors.managed)
formats.covers: role_colors.py reads and rewrites both: semicolon-separated nick:color pairs; 'managed' records the pairs it forced, so a renamed identity's forced color is removed
